title: Position Sizing
hook: Risk only what you can afford to lose. Size your position, not your ego.
mission: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to explain why the same setup can be smart at one size and reckless at another.

blocks.heading: Contracts change the money, not the structure

beats.heading: Weight, not quality
beats.body: Your entry can be clean and your stop loss can be correct, but if your size is too big, the trade becomes emotionally heavy.

beats.heading: The chart doesn't care
beats.body: Position sizing is what makes the same setup feel manageable or reckless — the chart doesn't know how many contracts you're in, but you will.

blocks.heading: Same setup, two different sizes
blocks.prompt: Tap each size to see how the same 10-point stop changes weight.

left.label: 1 contract
left.desc: 1 MNQ contract on a 10-point stop risks $20. Small, manageable, easy to think clearly through.

right.label: 10 contracts
right.desc: 10 MNQ contracts on the exact same 10-point stop risks $200 — the setup didn't change, the weight did.

blocks.heading: What's actually happening here?
blocks.scenario: After a loss, a trader doubles her next position size to "win it back faster."

options.label: Emotion is driving her sizing decision, not her risk plan
options.feedback: Exactly — that's revenge sizing, and it compounds risk right when discipline matters most.

options.label: That's a smart way to recover losses quickly
options.feedback: Increasing size to chase back a loss usually increases risk at the worst possible moment.

blocks.quote: Keep your size consistent. Going heavier because confidence is high, or doubling size after a loss, is emotion talking — not a risk plan.

questions.question: Two traders take the identical setup — same entry, same stop, same target — but one uses 1 contract and the other uses 10. Is one trade objectively better structured?
options: No — the structure is identical; only the dollar risk and emotional weight differ
Yes — more contracts always means a better trade
Yes — fewer contracts always means a safer, more valid setup
questions.why: Sizing decides how much is on the line — it doesn't change whether the setup itself is good.

questions.question: Your contract size should be decided by your ___, not by how confident or excited you feel today.
questions.why: A risk plan stays consistent regardless of how a trader feels in the moment.

takeaways: Position size decides how much dollar risk and emotional weight a trade carries.
The same setup can be reasonable at a small size and reckless at an oversized one.
Sizing should come from your risk plan, never from mood or a win/loss streak.
remember: Size your position, not your ego.
